text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- Finland's policy of working closely with NATO while refraining from membership will not change, says President Martti Ahtisaari who is schedueld to visit Russian President Boris Yeltsin this weekend at Yeltsin's summer cottage.
- Gold is losing importance as a hedge against inflation as international economies grow more stable, says the Bank of Finland's director of market operations Markus Fogelholm.
- Northern Finland may be too wealthy to qualify for European Union regional policy subsidies if the European Commission approves a proposed reform EU regional policy.
- One third of young Finns see nothing wrong with wage earners accepting undeclared extra income, a Central Organization of Finnish Trade Unions (SAK) poll shows.
- New Finnish opera on the life of 19th-century author Aleksis Kivi was warmly received at its world premiere in Savonlinna in eastern Finland.
KAUPPALEHTI
- The lumber industry may face an unsteady autumn: orders for sawn timber have declined since the spring, but sector representatives say there is still no reason to expect prices to fall.
- Pulp stocks in Finland and Sweden fell by 10,000 tonnes in June, Swedish consultancy Momentum says -- North American and Scandinavian (Norscan) June pulp stocks data due next week.
- Finnish Academy of Science plans a broad cross-disciplinary research programme on Finland's economic crisis of the early 1990s.
AAMULEHTI

- The European Commission's plans to reduce prices of farm produce and to restructure the subsidy system are impossible for a country like Finland where farming conditions are unfavourable, says Esa Harmala chairman of the Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners (MTK).
- Finnish companies have attracted increasing interest abroad, and foreigners have made 46 major investments in Finland in the last six years, unofficial statistics by Invest in Finland Bureau show.
TURUN SANOMAT
- The Swiss International Institute for Management ranked Finland the world's fourth most competitive country, up from 15th last year.
- Daily goods shops should not be allowed to sell medicines because it would hurt small pharmacies or hike drug prices, Social and Health Minister Sinikka Monkare says.
- Swedish municipalities eager to save on food costs are seeking contacts with the Finnish food industry in order to bypass big Swedish retailers.
DEMARI
- Regional inequality and migration from rural areas to urban centres are increasing, a study by the Association of Finnish Local and Regional Authorities shows.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
